Title: Neue effiziente Netzteile von Super Flower – Hartware
URL: https://www.hartware.de/2013/12/08/neue-effiziente-netzteile-von-super-flower/
Published: 2013-12-08T00:00:00.000Z
Author: 8. Dezember 2013
Highlights:
## 80Plus Gold ab 350 Watt und Platinum ab 650 Watt

 8. Dezember 2013, 11:11 von Thomas Ludziarczyk 

Caseking bietet ab sofort drei neue Super Flower Netzteilserien in seinem Shop an. Den Einstieg ins 80Plus-Gold-zertifizierte Segment bilden die Super Flower Golden Green HX (350 bis 750 Watt). Die kleinste Variante, das Golden Green HX 350W ist nach Huntkey Jumper R9 300W, FSP350-60EGN(90) 350W und SeaSonic G360 erst das vierte 80Plus-Gold-zertifizierte Netzteil mit einer geringeren Leistung als 400 Watt.

 Die Netzteile der Golden Green HX Serie bieten keine abnehmbaren Anschlüsse, aber selbst die leistungsfähigeren Modelle bleiben deshalb unter 100 Euro.

Für den High-End Bereich gibt es die neue 80Plus-Platin-zertifizierte Leadex Platinum Serie. Caseking bietet aber aktuell nur die für Multi-GPU Systeme interessanten Modelle mit 1000 und 1200 Watt an. Ob auch die kleineren Varianten mit 650 und 850 Watt den deutschen Markt erreichen, ist noch unbekannt. Alle Netzteile aus der Leadex Platinum Serie sind vollmodular und bieten LED-beleuchtete Anschlüsse.

Darüberhinaus gibt es mit dem Golden Silent 80Plus Gold Fanless ein weiteres lüfterloses Netzteil von Super Flower. Dieses unterscheidet sich aber stark von dem bisher gelisteten. Während das Platinum Fanless 500W einen massiven Aluminium-Kühlkörper besitzt, ist das neue Golden Silent 80Plus Gold Fanless mit 430 Watt Leistung optisch stark an die luftdurchlässige Fanless-Bauweise der SeaSonic X-Serie angelehnt.

Super Flower setzt bei all seinen Netzteilen auf eine „einzelne 12-Volt-Leitung“ und verspricht, die notwendigen Schutzschaltungen zu verbauen: Over Voltage Protection / Over Current Protection / Over Power Protection / Short Circuit Protection / Under Voltage Protection.

Alle Netzteile sind ab sofort bei Caseking gelistet und bis auf das erst Mitte Januar erwartete Fanless-Modell sofort erhältlich oder kurzfristig verfügbar. Die Preise:

- Golden Green HX Serie: 50 bis 100 Euro 
- Leadex Platinum 1000W: 190 Euro 
- Leadex Platinum 1200W: 220 Euro 
- Golden Silent 80Plus Gold Fanless 430W: 110 Euro

Published: 2014-03-15T15:08:38.000Z
Author: Borja Rodríguez
Highlights:
Super Flower lanza sus fuentes de alimentación Golden Green HX

# Super Flower lanza sus fuentes de alimentación Golden Green HX

Por Borja Rodríguez 15/03/2014 Hardware

Super Flower anunció el lanzamiento de su nueva serie de fuentes de alimentación Golden Green HX que, como deja entrever en su nombre, estamos delante de una serie dotada de una certificación energética 80 Plus Gold con una eficiencia energética de hasta un 92.03%. Pese a que comparte la misma nomenclatura HX vista en modelos de Corsair, las fuentes Super Flower Golden Green HX no son modulares, todas ellas cuentan con el cableado fijado dotado de un mallado y refrigeradas por medio de un ventilador de 120 mm.

Las características de las fuentes de alimentación Super Flower Golden Green HX se completan con protecciones OVP, OCP, OPP, SCP y UVP, certificados ATX 12V. V2.2, EPS 12V. V2.91 y SSI EPS 12V. V2.92, un PFC activo, soporte de configuraciones Nvidia SLI y AMD CrossFireX, y podemos verlas en España en capacidades de 350, 450 y 550W de potencia a un precio respectivo de 52, 58 y 68 euros.

Top review: This is a highly rated PSU. It easily powers a 5600x, RTX 3080 a few SSDs and 8 case fans. There are 3 switch positions in the back which can be set for fan curve. Leave it on silent to barely hear any noise at all. So awesome, I purchased another for my other PC.I nearly had a heart attack when I first tried to turn on my newly built (and fairly expensive) PC and... nothing happened. I had been very careful during the assembly to make sure that I was doing everything correctly, so I feared that one of my parts was bad. After some cursing and Googling, I found out how to do a "paper clip test" on the PSU, which confirmed that the PSU was functional. I then swapped out the power cable for another one, and at that point the PC booted up fine.Since then, it has been working without issue. Super Flower seems to have a generally good reputation for their component quality, so I'm not really concerned about running into any other issues with it. I could have done without the initial panic caused by the bad power cable though.Pros:* Good build quality* Good holdup time* Low ripple* Good transient response* Very quiet fan (even in non-eco mode); Lamda A+ rating on noise.* Nice looking sleeving on PCIe, EPS, and ATX cables* Stays cool even under heavy load* Worked 100% out of the box* Price (after -$30 coupon is fair; $120 for the 850 watt model. Other A-tier models were more.* Nice pouch for unused cables* Reasonably short on depth* Cable length is perfect for a mid-tower; if you have a larger case, you may want extensions* No problems on stress test (see full system specs* Just barely misses Platinum level efficency at 220. Misses by more at 110, but still exceeds Gold level by a healthy amount.* Good independent reviews.Cons:* Cables have caps in them. A plus for ripple, but a minus on appearance.* PCIe cables are pigtailed; I prefer one connector per cable.* Other than where the caps are, the cables are really slim; it is fine from an appearance point of view, but I wonder if they are really using 18ga wire.Overall review/system specs:Gigabyte X570 MasterRyzen 7 5800XPatriot 4400 MT/s DRAM 8g x 4, Running at 15-15-15-15-32 3800MT/sPowerColor Liquid Devil 6800XTWD BLack SN850 500GB x2Sabrent Rocket 1TBWD Black 6TB HDDCustom loop with two 360mm radiators8xNoctua Redux 1700RPM PWM fansCPU and GPU both highly overclocked, total system draw at max (excluding short spikes): about 600wPhanteks Pro 2 caseSo, obviously a high end system with very demanding power draw with some heavy transients. I trust this PSU with my system, so obviously I have a lot of confidence in this PSU. I was going to go with a Coesair RMX850x or a Seasonic PX-850, but they were both $160 at my time of purchase and this was $120. All three of these PSUs are top picks in the A-tier on the LTT PSU tier list.Bottom line: I am picky with my components and I am pleased with this PSU.***READ THE NEWEST UPDATE***The fan is honestly quite loud once it kicks in. Initially, I didn't think that this would be an issue because I expected it to only need the fan under heavy load. However, even just browsing the internet or doing some light work it will occasionally spin up for about 30 seconds. A small nitpick, but with an NH-D15, Noctua case fans, and a pretty quiet fan curve, it kinda kills the vibe. The noise level is comparable to the 3.5 inch HDD also in the build which also kills the quiet vibe.Obviously, this isn't an issue when gaming or doing more intensive work because everything else is gonna be a little louder and just drown it out. I also compared it to my previous 600W 80+ EVGA unit and the fan on that is near silent despite running 24/7.It looks cool, no dumb lights, whatever glass panels are silly anyways. Legendary brand reputation, good warranty, and I trust this thing to last and work just as it should for years to come. The cable length is adequate for any case I've ever seen and short enough to tuck away pretty nicely in my FT03. The cables come in a nice little velcro bag. Dunno if that's industry standard but it's cool.Overall I'd still recommend this unit. If the fan was quieter it would be 5 stars no problem. But if you're really prioritizing silence, do a little more research than I did.EDIT 1: I'm dumb. It's really best to just leave the fan in 24/7 mode instead of allowing it to ramp up to crazy high speeds only when it's getting too hot. BUT even at a constant low RPM it really isn't very quiet so my 4 star still stands.EDIT 2: I'm double dumb. Turns out having a fixed voltage on my CPU for its overclock makes everything hot and makes the PSU work harder than it needs to at idle, therefore spinning the fan faster in the constant mode. Updated to 5 stars. After setting up adaptive voltage, I only notice an increase in noise when I'm in my case flipping the switch from active to passive and listening for it.Ok I will say I love this PSU and when I got it in Oct 2020 was when PSU prices was crazy and a 850W gold was going for 200 or more and hard to find plus I got it for $166.99 because Tech Deals and LTT on YouTube Recommended it. It has 3 fans modes one being ECO Fanless & Silent Mode being the other 2 based off power usage. I use silent 🤫 mode 1 and you can't hear it, with it right on my desk next to me and I love the energy efficiency.CON: it is not well known lol but it should be and I believe at one time they We're making EVGA SuperNOVA before they moved on to another company, and Super Flower started using their own name.this psu is very good for the price. at first it did not arrive and seller was very accommodating and send another unit with no questions asked.This PSU works great in my Dell XPS 8910. Didn't have any issue with fitting PSU inside my pc at all. I recommend this PSU for anybody who has a Dell XPS machine. Like this PSU a lot better than EVGA.My son built his own PC and is impressed with this.Really easy to install, has everything included to wire up pc.✅ Recensione in Breve:Prodotto tra i più validi in commercio in termini di stabilità delle linee e sicurezza. A parità di prezzo con altri prodotti (escludendo alcune piattaforme Seasonic) vince a mani basse. Considerabile ad un prezzo non superiore ai 100 euro.✅ Recensione Estesa:Per chi è già pratico del mondo delle configurazioni pc, questa recensione potrebbe essere del tutto inutile, e non farò una descrizione tecnica dettagliata (vi rimando alla scheda tecnica sul sito del produttore per quella!). Tuttavia mi sembra doveroso spiegare a chi ne sa poco e nulla quanto questo prodotto potrebbe fare la differenza tra una configurazione ben riuscita, ed una che durerà poco tempo. La farfallina che ho citato nel titolo, è forse un marchio sconosciuto ai più. Trattasi del brand Super Flower, azienda cinese specializzata da oltre venti anni nella fabbricazione di alimentatori. Questa informazione da sola non basta a rendere giustizia a quella che viene annoverata tra le migliori aziende al mondo per la produzione di queste componenti: se siete fan del marchio EVGA, vi farà piacere sapere che molte piattaforme dei loro alimentatori più recenti sono della suddetta Super Flower, questo a garanzia della bontà dei prodotti, e della serietà dell’azienda stessa. Messe in chiaro le credenziali di presentazione del Brand Super Flower, passo a dire che per il ponte principale, è usata componentistica giapponese, mentre per il ponte secondario abbiamo componenti taiwanesi. Ora, questo potrebbe significare tutto e niente per voi, quindi proverò a spiegarlo in parole più semplici: ciò che ho detto nella frase precedente, si traduce in ottima stabilità sia della linea principale a 12V che di quelle secondarie a 3V e 5V; in parole ancora più povere, avrete un prodotto che manda corrente alle vostre componenti in maniera egregia, e che a meno di beccare un esemplare fallato, non vi darà mai problemi. La soppressione del Ripple è ottima (il ripple è un “rumore” sulle linee che sporca il passaggio della corrente, e che porta a danneggiare le componenti. E qualora ve lo steste chiedendo, è un parametro imprescindibile, non può essere eliminato, ma solo soppresso quanto più possibile!), cosa da non sottovalutare mai durante la scelta di un alimentatore. Per riassumere questa recensione in una sola frase: “Se costa meno di 100 euro, e 550W sono sufficienti per la configurazione, puoi comprarlo ad occhi chiusi!”. Come ripeto sempre a chiunque mi affidi una configurazione, non transigo mai sulla scelta dell’alimentatore: la mediocrità, in questo caso, danneggia solamente. Non si tratta di essere affezionati ad un marchio piuttosto che ad un altro, ma di esser sicuri di ciò che si sta comprando. Ci sono davvero pochi altri alimentatori capaci di competere con questo sulla stessa fascia di prezzo, e per una componente così delicata ed importante allo stesso tempo, affidarsi ad un brand che venda certezze è il minimo indispensabile. Per tanto consiglio l’acquisto di questo alimentatore senza remore. Al pari di Seasonic, è una soluzione che raramente delude!-IvanLovely bit of kit. Modular design, so no excess cables to hide.Ich habe ein recht stromhungriges System. Bestehend aus einem Intel 9900K und einer Vega 64 LC. Mein vorheriges 850W Netzteil (gekauft Anfang diesen Jahres) schaltete den PC immer wieder in Situationen ab in denen die Grafikkarte in eine Lastwechsel Situation kam. Da ich einen Defekt vermute geht mein "altes" Netzteil in die RMA.Als Ersatz habe ich mir das Super Flower Leadex III mit ebenfalls 850W bestellt. Seit dem Einbau dieses Netzteils habe ich keine Abschaltung mehr gesehen, obwohl ich es durch Testprogramme wirklich provoziert habe. Für mich bleibt das Super Flower bis auf weiteres, da es mir wirklich ein Problem gelöst hat.
